claim: The authenticated publish API permits an attacker-controlled HTTPS Git destination, including private-network or metadata hosts, and sends optional git credentials to that destination.
trigger: An authenticated caller submits POST /api/artifacts (or the authenticated update/version paths) with git_url set to an HTTPS URL resolving to an internal service or attacker-controlled host; when git_token is supplied, _clone constructs a credentialed URL and invokes git clone against it.
impact: The service makes outbound connections to arbitrary HTTPS hosts from its network context, enabling SSRF probing/access to internal services reachable over HTTPS; a caller-provided git_token is placed in URL userinfo and can be disclosed to an attacker-controlled Git endpoint (and Git's outbound request path).

evidence.detail: src/builder.py:578-598 constructs argv with clone_url and runs git clone; src/main.py:943-950 passes request body git_url, git_username, and git_token into build_from_git.
src/main.py:676-710 advertises git_url as any HTTPS repository and accepts a transient git_token; no host, IP, DNS, or egress policy is specified.
src/main.py:1800-1827 and 1928+ authenticate management publish/update/version flows before calling _build, so the attacker only needs a valid management token.

expected_behavior_source: The public Git publishing contract in src/main.py:676-710 and skills/artifact-publisher/SKILL.md permits repository cloning, but does not authorize access to private-network destinations or forwarding caller credentials to arbitrary hosts; the security boundary requires destination/egress restriction when accepting user-supplied URLs.
suggested_fix: Restrict Git destinations to an explicit approved-host policy and resolve/revalidate addresses against private, loopback, link-local, and metadata ranges before connecting; avoid sending git_token unless the destination is approved, and disable unsafe redirect/rebinding paths.
